hints.title: Parity Invariant
hints.text: Examine small game values of n. If n is even, Alice can subtract 1 to hand an odd number to Bob. An odd number has only odd factors, forcing Bob to return an even number.

hints.title: Forced Winning Strategy
hints.text: Alice can maintain the invariant that she always receives even numbers and always hands odd numbers. Eventually, Bob is handed the number 1 and has no valid move.

hints.title: Constant Evaluation
hints.text: Because Alice starts with an even number whenever n is even and optimal play preserves this parity state, Alice wins if and only if n % 2 == 0.

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating full game-tree minimax takes exponential or O(N^2) dynamic programming time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Mathematical parity induction resolves the game in constant time and zero memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize the game theory parity invariant or deduce it via small examples.
complexity.notes: Alice wins for all even n and loses for all odd n under optimal play.
